5	/// Decides *when* the saved session is written (issue #46). `SessionStore` owns the file;
6	/// `AppStore+Session` owns what one window contributes; this owns coalescing, the restore gate, and
7	/// the quit freeze.
8	///
9	/// There is exactly one writer, and it rebuilds the whole document from every live window. That
10	/// replaces `AppStore.persistsSidebarPrefs` arbitration *for the session only*: that gate exists
11	/// because a single `Defaults` key cannot hold N windows — this file can. `persistsSidebarPrefs`
12	/// still governs the Defaults keys it always did.
13	@MainActor
14	final class SessionCoordinator {
15	  static let shared = SessionCoordinator(store: .forCurrentEnvironment())
16	
17	  /// Coalescing window. Long enough that a burst of layout edits costs one write.
18	  static let defaultDebounce: TimeInterval = 1
19	  /// **The ceiling is not an optimisation — it is what makes saving work at all.**
20	  ///
21	  /// The dirty sources publish faster than 1 Hz whenever a terminal is doing anything:
22	  /// `TerminalSessions.pulsePaneActivity` bumps a `@Published` dict per activity report, and every
23	  /// live-title/cwd/progress update reassigns `tabsByTarget` (`TerminalTab` is a value type). A plain
24	  /// cancel-and-replace debounce therefore has its deadline pushed out forever while output streams,
25	  /// and **never fires** — so splitting a pane beside a running dev server would never be saved.
26	  ///
27	  /// Recording when the session FIRST went dirty and forcing a write once this much time has passed
28	  /// bounds the loss regardless of how chatty the terminals are.
29	  static let defaultCeiling: TimeInterval = 5
30	
31	  private let store: SessionStore
32	  private let debounce: TimeInterval
33	  private let ceiling: TimeInterval
34	  private let capture: () -> [WindowSession]
35	  /// Writes each live pane's scrollback into the store (issue #144). Separate from `capture` because
36	  /// it runs ONLY at quit: reading every pane's history is far too heavy for a coalesced save.
37	  private let captureScrollback: (SessionStore) -> Void
38	  private let logger = Logger(
39	    subsystem: "com.developwithstyle.workroom", category: "session")
40	
41	  private var pending: DispatchWorkItem?
42	  /// When the current dirty streak began — the ceiling is measured from here, not from the last edit.
43	  private var dirtySince: Date?
44	  /// The last document written, compared with `==` rather than a hash: Swift seeds `hashValue` per
45	  /// process, and a collision would silently suppress a write the user needs.
46	  private var lastWritten: [WindowSession]?
47	  /// Depth rather than a flag so nested suspensions (several windows restoring) cannot resume early.
48	  private var suspensions = 0
49	  private var dirtyWhileSuspended = false
50	  /// Set once the app is genuinely terminating. Windows close one by one during a quit, and the
51	  /// document is rebuilt from the LIVE windows — without this, the last window closing would
52	  /// overwrite a good session with an empty one after the flush already wrote it.
53	  private var isFrozen = false
54	
55	  init(
56	    store: SessionStore = SessionStore(),
57	    debounce: TimeInterval = SessionCoordinator.defaultDebounce,
58	    ceiling: TimeInterval = SessionCoordinator.defaultCeiling,
59	    capture: (() -> [WindowSession])? = nil,
60	    captureScrollback: ((SessionStore) -> Void)? = nil
61	  ) {
62	    self.store = store
63	    self.debounce = debounce
64	    self.ceiling = ceiling
65	    self.capture = capture ?? { WindowRegistry.shared.captureSessionWindows() }
66	    self.captureScrollback =
67	      captureScrollback ?? { store in
68	        for appStore in WindowRegistry.shared.allStores { appStore.captureScrollback(into: store) }
69	      }
70	  }
71	
72	  /// Exposed so a caller can tell "no session" from "a session this build must not touch".
73	  var writesDisabled: Bool { store.writesDisabled }
74	
75	  // MARK: Restore gate
76	
77	  /// True while a restore is in flight, so nothing writes a half-restored document.
78	  var isSuspended: Bool { suspensions > 0 }
79	
80	  /// Stop writing until the matching `resumeSaves()`.
81	  ///
82	  /// **This is the gate that stops the launch window deleting the others.** Restoring window 1
83	  /// mutates `TerminalSessions` and `AppStore`, which marks the session dirty. If that write landed
84	  /// before the sibling windows had opened and registered, the document would be rebuilt from the one
85	  /// live window and overwrite the file — silently discarding windows 2 and 3 on the very launch that
86	  /// was meant to bring them back.
87	  func suspendSaves() {
88	    suspensions += 1
89	    pending?.cancel()
90	    pending = nil
91	  }
92	
93	  func resumeSaves() {
94	    guard suspensions > 0 else { return }
95	    suspensions -= 1
96	    guard suspensions == 0, dirtyWhileSuspended else { return }
97	    dirtyWhileSuspended = false
98	    markDirty()
99	  }
100	
101	  // MARK: Dirty tracking
102	
103	  /// The session changed. Safe to call at any rate — this is called from publishers that fire many
104	  /// times a second.
105	  func markDirty() {
106	    guard !isFrozen, !store.writesDisabled else { return }
107	    guard !isSuspended else {
108	      dirtyWhileSuspended = true
109	      return
110	    }
111	
112	    let now = Date()
113	    let start = dirtySince ?? now
114	    dirtySince = start
115	
116	    // Past the ceiling, write now rather than pushing the deadline out again.
117	    if now.timeIntervalSince(start) >= ceiling {
118	      writeIfChanged()
119	      return
120	    }
121	
122	    pending?.cancel()
123	    let work = DispatchWorkItem { [weak self] in
124	      MainActor.assumeIsolated { self?.writeIfChanged() }
125	    }
126	    pending = work
127	    DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + debounce, execute: work)
128	  }
129	
130	  /// Capture and persist immediately if anything actually changed. Also the ceiling's landing point.
131	  func writeIfChanged() {
132	    pending?.cancel()
133	    pending = nil
134	    dirtySince = nil
135	    guard !isFrozen, !store.writesDisabled, !isSuspended else { return }
136	
137	    let windows = capture()
138	    guard windows != lastWritten else { return }
139	    lastWritten = windows
140	    store.write(makeFile(windows))
141	  }
142	
143	  // MARK: Quit
144	
145	  /// Capture and write **synchronously**, then stop writing for the rest of the process.
146	  ///
147	  /// Called past the quit confirmation — never above it. A cancelled ⌘Q must leave saving fully
148	  /// working, so this cannot run anywhere a user can still say "no".
149	  func flushAndFreeze() {
150	    guard !isFrozen else { return }
151	    pending?.cancel()
152	    pending = nil
153	    dirtySince = nil
154	    // Suspended means a restore never finished; the live windows are not the user's session, so
155	    // writing them now would replace a good file with a partial one.
156	    if !store.writesDisabled && !isSuspended {
157	      let windows = capture()
158	      lastWritten = windows
159	      store.writeSynchronously(makeFile(windows))
160	      // Scrollback is captured HERE and nowhere else (issue #144): quitting is the one moment worth
161	      // reading every pane's history for. Prune afterwards, unconditionally, so a pane that captured
162	      // nothing this time loses its old sidecar rather than restoring yesterday's output.
163	      captureScrollback(store)
164	      store.pruneScrollback(keeping: Self.tabKeys(in: windows))
165	    }
166	    isFrozen = true
167	  }
168	
169	  // MARK: Read
170	
171	  func read() -> SessionStore.ReadOutcome { store.read() }
172	
173	  /// A restored pane's saved text, for replay (issue #144).
174	  func scrollback(forTabKey key: String) -> String? { store.readScrollback(forTabKey: key) }
175	
176	  /// Every tab key in the document, which is exactly the set of sidecars worth keeping.
177	  private static func tabKeys(in windows: [WindowSession]) -> Set<String> {
178	    Set(windows.flatMap { $0.targets.flatMap { $0.tabs.map(\.key) } })
179	  }
180	
181	  private func makeFile(_ windows: [WindowSession]) -> SessionFile {
182	    SessionFile(
183	      savedAt: Date(),
184	      appVersion: Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleShortVersionString") as? String,
185	      windows: windows)
186	  }
187	}

190	  /// Every live window's contribution to the saved session, in a stable order so an unchanged layout
191	  /// produces an unchanged document (and therefore no write).
192	  func captureSessionWindows() -> [WindowSession] {
193	    allStores
194	      .sorted { $0.windowNumber < $1.windowNumber }
195	      .map { $0.captureWindowSession() }
196	  }
197	}

3	/// The on-disk shape of a saved session — the open panels, split layouts, and windows restored on
4	/// the next launch (issue #46). Written by `SessionStore` to
5	/// `Application Support/Workroom/<bundle id>/session.json`.
6	///
7	/// **Every type here is a hand-written mirror.** No runtime type (`PaneLayout`, `TerminalTab`,
8	/// `SidebarID`, the content descriptors) gains `Codable`, so the file format is never hostage to an
9	/// internal field rename — the same stored-data-contract rule `RunConfig` carries in
10	/// `DefaultsKeys.swift`. The field names below ARE the contract; renaming one silently invalidates
11	/// every user's saved session.
12	///
13	/// # Versioning rule — read before bumping `schemaVersion`
14	///
15	/// **Additive changes NEVER bump `schemaVersion`.** Adding a tab kind, or adding an optional field,
16	/// is additive. Only a breaking reshape bumps.
17	///
18	/// This is what makes the lossy decoding below load-bearing rather than decorative: a Nightly build
19	/// writes a fifth tab kind, the user rolls back to stable, and stable drops that one tab while
20	/// restoring everything else. Bump the version for an additive kind and the whole file is discarded
21	/// before the lossy path ever runs — deleting every user's session for no reason.
22	///
23	/// The same split the app already draws between versioning a key (`inspector.layout.v2`) and
24	/// reconciling a shape (`AppStore.reconcileInspectorState`): version to discard, reconcile to keep.
25	///
26	/// A **newer** `schemaVersion` is read-only: restore nothing AND write nothing for that run, or an
27	/// older build silently destroys a newer one's session on its next save. Three build identities ship
28	/// side by side (Workroom, Workroom Dev, Workroom Nightly), so that rollback is a real path.
29	///
30	/// # What is deliberately absent
31	///
32	/// - **The PTY and child processes.** A restored terminal is a fresh login shell in the remembered
33	///   directory; the process it was running is gone. (Its *text* does come back — scrollback lives in
34	///   sidecar files beside this document, never inside it. See `SessionStore` and issue #144.)
35	/// - **Run tabs.** Restoring one would resurrect a dev server with no `AppStore.RunState` behind it —
36	///   an untracked process orphaned on its port, the failure `WindowRegistry.runOwner(for:excluding:)`
37	///   and issue #7 exist to prevent. `Defaults[.runCommands]` already survives, and `RunConfig.autoRun`
38	///   is the deliberate opt-in.
39	/// - **`liveTitle` / `progressActive` / activity pulses.** Display state about a process that no
40	///   longer exists. Excluding them is also what keeps the save digest stable: a terminal animating
41	///   its title produces a byte-identical snapshot, so it costs a comparison and no disk write.
42	/// - **Navigation history.** Its entries key on tab ids, which restore re-mints by design.
43	
44	// MARK: - Limits
45	
46	/// Bounds on what a session file may ask the app to allocate at launch. These are a real ceiling,
47	/// not decoration: restore materialises every target's tab models eagerly (the sidebar's terminal
48	/// subtree renders from them), so a hostile or corrupt file could otherwise allocate tens of
49	/// thousands of views before the first frame. Anything dropped is logged — silent truncation reads
50	/// as full coverage.
51	enum SessionLimits {
52	  static let maxWindows = 8
53	  static let maxTargetsPerWindow = 20
54	  static let maxTabsPerTarget = 20
55	  /// Split trees are user-built by repeated ⌘D; a dozen levels is far past any real layout, and the
56	  /// cap is what stops a hand-edited file recursing `materialize` into the stack.
57	  static let maxSplitDepth = 12
58	  /// Refused before decoding — array caps bound element *counts*, not the size of one giant string.
59	  static let maxFileBytes = 512 * 1024
60	  /// Clamps paths, titles, and commit ids individually.
61	  static let maxStringLength = 4096
62	  /// Per-pane scrollback kept in a sidecar file (issue #144). The value is overwhelmingly at the
63	  /// recent end, and a cap keeps the quit path bounded no matter how much a pane logged.
64	  static let maxScrollbackBytes = 256 * 1024
65	  /// A sidecar larger than this on disk is corrupt by definition — twice the cap, so a legitimate
66	  /// file can never trip it.
67	  static let maxScrollbackFileBytes = 512 * 1024
68	}

70	// MARK: - Lossy array decoding
71	
72	/// An array that drops the elements it cannot decode instead of failing the whole document.
73	///
74	/// This is the single most valuable primitive in the schema: it turns "a newer build wrote a tab kind
75	/// this build has never heard of" from *your entire session is gone* into *one tab is missing*. It
76	/// only pays because additive changes do not bump `schemaVersion` (see the file header) — otherwise
77	/// the envelope check discards the file before any element is examined.
78	@propertyWrapper
79	struct Lossy<Element: Codable & Sendable>: Codable, Sendable {
80	  var wrappedValue: [Element]
81	
82	  init(wrappedValue: [Element]) { self.wrappedValue = wrappedValue }
83	
84	  /// Consumes exactly one element of any shape. Decoding a *failed* element does not advance an
85	  /// `UnkeyedDecodingContainer`, so a permissive type has to consume it or the loop never progresses.
86	  private struct AnyElement: Decodable {
87	    init(from decoder: Decoder) throws { _ = decoder }
88	  }
89	
90	  init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
91	    var container = try decoder.unkeyedContainer()
92	    var decoded: [Element] = []
93	    while !container.isAtEnd {
94	      let indexBefore = container.currentIndex
95	      do {
96	        decoded.append(try container.decode(Element.self))
97	      } catch {
98	        _ = try? container.decode(AnyElement.self)
99	      }
100	      // Belt and braces: if neither the decode nor the skip advanced the cursor, stop rather than
101	      // spin forever on a container shape we did not anticipate.
102	      if container.currentIndex == indexBefore { break }
103	    }
104	    wrappedValue = decoded
105	  }
106	
107	  func encode(to encoder: Encoder) throws {
108	    var container = encoder.unkeyedContainer()
109	    for element in wrappedValue { try container.encode(element) }
110	  }
111	}
112	
113	extension Lossy: Equatable where Element: Equatable {}
114	extension Lossy: Hashable where Element: Hashable {}
115	
116	extension KeyedDecodingContainer {
117	  /// Makes an absent lossy array decode to empty rather than throwing, so a field added in a later
118	  /// version is readable by a build that predates it.
119	  func decode<T>(_ type: Lossy<T>.Type, forKey key: Key) throws -> Lossy<T> {
120	    try decodeIfPresent(type, forKey: key) ?? Lossy(wrappedValue: [])
121	  }
122	}

126	/// The Codable mirror of `PaneLayout`, generic over its leaf address (a tab key, or a target-id
127	/// string for the workroom split). Hand-written with an explicit `kind` discriminator so the on-disk
128	/// format is a contract THIS file owns, not whatever Swift synthesises for an indirect enum with
129	/// associated values.
130	///
131	/// `PaneLayout`'s per-split `UUID` is deliberately NOT persisted: it addresses a divider during a
132	/// drag and nothing refers to it across a launch. `materialize` mints a fresh one.
133	indirect enum LayoutNode<Leaf: Codable & Hashable & Sendable>: Codable, Hashable, Sendable {
134	  case leaf(Leaf)
135	  case split(orientation: String, ratio: Double, first: LayoutNode, second: LayoutNode)
136	
137	  static var horizontal: String { "horizontal" }
138	  static var vertical: String { "vertical" }
139	
140	  private enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
141	    case kind, leaf, orientation, ratio, first, second
142	  }
143	  private enum Kind: String, Codable {
144	    case leaf, split
145	  }
146	
147	  init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
148	    let container = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
149	    switch try container.decode(Kind.self, forKey: .kind) {
150	    case .leaf:
151	      self = .leaf(try container.decode(Leaf.self, forKey: .leaf))
152	    case .split:
153	      self = .split(
154	        orientation: try container.decode(String.self, forKey: .orientation),
155	        ratio: try container.decode(Double.self, forKey: .ratio),
156	        first: try container.decode(LayoutNode.self, forKey: .first),
157	        second: try container.decode(LayoutNode.self, forKey: .second))
158	    }
159	  }
160	
161	  func encode(to encoder: Encoder) throws {
162	    var container = encoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
163	    switch self {
164	    case .leaf(let leaf):
165	      try container.encode(Kind.leaf, forKey: .kind)
166	      try container.encode(leaf, forKey: .leaf)
167	    case .split(let orientation, let ratio, let first, let second):
168	      try container.encode(Kind.split, forKey: .kind)
169	      try container.encode(orientation, forKey: .orientation)
170	      try container.encode(ratio, forKey: .ratio)
171	      try container.encode(first, forKey: .first)
172	      try container.encode(second, forKey: .second)
173	    }
174	  }
175	
176	  /// Every leaf address in reading order — the counterpart of `PaneLayout.tabIDs`, used to validate
177	  /// a decoded tree against the tabs that actually survived.
178	  var leaves: [Leaf] {
179	    switch self {
180	    case .leaf(let leaf): return [leaf]
181	    case .split(_, _, let first, let second): return first.leaves + second.leaves
182	    }
183	  }
184	
185	  /// Depth of the deepest split, so a hand-edited tree can be rejected before `materialize` walks it.
186	  var depth: Int {
187	    switch self {
188	    case .leaf: return 1
189	    case .split(_, _, let first, let second): return 1 + max(first.depth, second.depth)
190	    }
191	  }
192	}

194	extension LayoutNode {
195	  /// Runtime tree → snapshot tree. `address` maps a runtime leaf to its persisted key; a leaf that
196	  /// maps to nil is dropped and its parent collapses to the surviving sibling — the same collapse
197	  /// rule as `PaneLayout.removingLeaf`.
198	  ///
199	  /// Returns nil when fewer than two leaves survive, mirroring `materialize`: a lone leaf is not a
200	  /// split, and writing one would put a shape in the file that the live model cannot hold. Excluding
201	  /// a run tab from a two-pane split is exactly this case.
202	  static func capture<L: Hashable>(
203	    _ layout: PaneLayout<L>, address: (L) -> Leaf?
204	  ) -> LayoutNode? {
205	    guard let tree = captureNode(layout, address: address) else { return nil }
206	    guard case .split = tree else { return nil }
207	    return tree
208	  }
209	
210	  private static func captureNode<L: Hashable>(
211	    _ layout: PaneLayout<L>, address: (L) -> Leaf?
212	  ) -> LayoutNode? {
213	    switch layout {
214	    case .leaf(let id):
215	      return address(id).map { .leaf($0) }
216	    case .split(_, let orientation, let ratio, let first, let second):
217	      let capturedFirst = captureNode(first, address: address)
218	      let capturedSecond = captureNode(second, address: address)
219	      switch (capturedFirst, capturedSecond) {
220	      case (let first?, let second?):
221	        return .split(
222	          orientation: orientation == .horizontal ? horizontal : vertical,
223	          ratio: Double(ratio), first: first, second: second)
224	      // A split with one surviving child is not a split — it IS that child (`PaneLayout`'s
225	      // "a lone leaf is not a split" invariant, enforced at the boundary rather than left to callers).
226	      case (let only?, nil), (nil, let only?):
227	        return only
228	      case (nil, nil):
229	        return nil
230	      }
231	    }
232	  }
233	
234	  /// Snapshot tree → runtime tree. `resolve` maps a persisted key to a live leaf; unresolvable leaves
235	  /// collapse into their sibling. Returns nil when fewer than two leaves survive, so a caller can
236	  /// never be handed a one-leaf "split".
237	  func materialize<L: Hashable>(_ resolve: (Leaf) -> L?) -> PaneLayout<L>? {
238	    guard let tree = materializeNode(resolve, depth: 0) else { return nil }
239	    guard case .split = tree else { return nil }
240	    return tree
241	  }
242	
243	  private func materializeNode<L: Hashable>(
244	    _ resolve: (Leaf) -> L?, depth: Int
245	  ) -> PaneLayout<L>? {
246	    guard depth < SessionLimits.maxSplitDepth else { return nil }
247	    switch self {
248	    case .leaf(let key):
249	      return resolve(key).map { .leaf($0) }
250	    case .split(let orientation, let ratio, let first, let second):
251	      guard let resolvedOrientation = Self.orientation(from: orientation) else { return nil }
252	      let resolvedFirst = first.materializeNode(resolve, depth: depth + 1)
253	      let resolvedSecond = second.materializeNode(resolve, depth: depth + 1)
254	      switch (resolvedFirst, resolvedSecond) {
255	      case (let first?, let second?):
256	        return .split(
257	          id: UUID(), orientation: resolvedOrientation,
258	          ratio: PaneRatio.sanitize(CGFloat(ratio)), first: first, second: second)
259	      case (let only?, nil), (nil, let only?):
260	        return only
261	      case (nil, nil):
262	        return nil
263	      }
264	    }
265	  }
266	
267	  /// An unrecognised orientation rejects the split (its tabs survive as solo panes) rather than
268	  /// guessing a layout the user never chose.
269	  private static func orientation(from raw: String) -> SplitOrientation? {
270	    switch raw {
271	    case horizontal: return .horizontal
272	    case vertical: return .vertical
273	    default: return nil
274	    }
275	  }
276	}

494	/// What `sanitized()` threw away, so the caller can log it. Caps and validation that drop work
495	/// silently read as full coverage — this is what stops that.
496	struct SessionSanitizeReport: Equatable {
497	  var droppedWindows = 0
498	  var droppedTargets = 0
499	  var droppedTabs = 0
500	  var droppedSplits = 0
501	
502	  var isEmpty: Bool {
503	    droppedWindows == 0 && droppedTargets == 0 && droppedTabs == 0 && droppedSplits == 0
504	  }
505	
506	  var summary: String {
507	    "windows: \(droppedWindows), targets: \(droppedTargets), tabs: \(droppedTabs), "
508	      + "splits: \(droppedSplits)"

512	extension SessionFile {
513	  /// Enforce every structural invariant restore depends on, and report what that cost.
514	  ///
515	  /// Array caps bound element *counts*; they do nothing about a hostile or corrupt *shape*. The real
516	  /// hazard is duplicate keys: restore builds dictionaries from `windowKey` / `targetID` / tab `key`,
517	  /// so a duplicate would silently redirect a split leaf or the focus to the wrong pane — a
518	  /// wrong-content bug with no crash to point at. First occurrence wins; the rest are dropped.
519	  ///
520	  /// Pure and `nonisolated`, so it is unit-testable without an `AppStore`, a window, or a file —
521	  /// the shape `AppStore.reconcileInspectorState` established.
522	  func sanitized() -> (file: SessionFile, report: SessionSanitizeReport) {
523	    var report = SessionSanitizeReport()
524	    var seenWindowKeys = Set<String>()
525	    var windows: [WindowSession] = []
526	
527	    for window in self.windows {
528	      guard windows.count < SessionLimits.maxWindows else {
529	        report.droppedWindows += 1
530	        continue
531	      }
532	      guard seenWindowKeys.insert(window.windowKey).inserted else {
533	        report.droppedWindows += 1
534	        continue
535	      }
536	      windows.append(window.sanitized(into: &report))
537	    }
538	
539	    var sanitized = self
540	    sanitized.windows = windows
541	    return (sanitized, report)
542	  }
543	}

545	extension WindowSession {
546	  fileprivate func sanitized(into report: inout SessionSanitizeReport) -> WindowSession {
547	    var seenTargetIDs = Set<String>()
548	    var targets: [TargetSession] = []
549	
550	    for target in self.targets {
551	      guard targets.count < SessionLimits.maxTargetsPerWindow else {
552	        report.droppedTargets += 1
553	        continue
554	      }
555	      guard seenTargetIDs.insert(target.targetID).inserted else {
556	        report.droppedTargets += 1
557	        continue
558	      }
559	      guard let sanitized = target.sanitized(into: &report) else {
560	        report.droppedTargets += 1
561	        continue
562	      }
563	      targets.append(sanitized)
564	    }
565	
566	    // A workroom-split group needs two or more distinct leaves to be a group at all, and a tree
567	    // deeper than the cap is rejected whole rather than walked.
568	    var splits: [LayoutNode<String>] = []
569	    for split in workroomSplits {
570	      let leaves = split.leaves
571	      guard split.depth <= SessionLimits.maxSplitDepth, leaves.count >= 2,
572	        Set(leaves).count == leaves.count
573	      else {
574	        report.droppedSplits += 1
575	        continue
576	      }
577	      splits.append(split)
578	    }
579	
580	    var window = self
581	    window.targets = targets
582	    window.workroomSplits = splits
583	    window.frame = frame.map { String($0.prefix(SessionLimits.maxStringLength)) }
584	    window.selectedTargetID = selectedTargetID.map {
585	      String($0.prefix(SessionLimits.maxStringLength))
586	    }
587	    window.expandedTargets = expandedTargets.map { expanded in
588	      Array(Set(expanded)).sorted().map { String($0.prefix(SessionLimits.maxStringLength)) }
589	    }
590	    return window
591	  }
592	}

594	extension TargetSession {
595	  /// Nil when nothing usable survives — never an empty target, which would make
596	  /// `TerminalSessions.ensureTab`'s "has this target been seeded?" check lie.
597	  fileprivate func sanitized(into report: inout SessionSanitizeReport) -> TargetSession? {
598	    var seenKeys = Set<String>()
599	    var tabs: [TabSession] = []
600	    var sawPreview = false
601	
602	    for tab in self.tabs {
603	      guard tabs.count < SessionLimits.maxTabsPerTarget else {
604	        report.droppedTabs += 1
605	        continue
606	      }
607	      guard tab.isWellFormed, seenKeys.insert(tab.key).inserted else {
608	        report.droppedTabs += 1
609	        continue
610	      }
611	      var tab = tab.clamped()
612	      // At most one preview tab per target (`TerminalSessions.previewTabID`). A hand-edited file
613	      // with two would give the target two italic chips and an ambiguous retarget slot; keep the
614	      // first and persist the rest.
615	      if tab.isPreview {
616	        if sawPreview {
617	          tab.clearPreview()
618	        } else {
619	          sawPreview = true
620	        }
621	      }
622	      tabs.append(tab)
623	    }
624	
625	    guard !tabs.isEmpty else { return nil }
626	
627	    let liveKeys = Set(tabs.map(\.key))
628	    var split = self.split
629	    if let candidate = split {
630	      let leaves = candidate.leaves
631	      let resolvable = leaves.filter { liveKeys.contains($0) }
632	      if candidate.depth > SessionLimits.maxSplitDepth || Set(leaves).count != leaves.count
633	        || resolvable.count < 2
634	      {
635	        // The split does not survive, but its tabs do — they simply render as solo panes.
636	        report.droppedSplits += 1
637	        split = nil
638	      }
639	    }
640	
641	    var target = self
642	    target.tabs = tabs
643	    target.split = split
644	    target.focusedKey = focusedKey.flatMap { liveKeys.contains($0) ? $0 : nil }
645	    target.targetID = String(targetID.prefix(SessionLimits.maxStringLength))
646	    return target
647	  }
648	}
